The model is a set of self-contained C++ headers. **They use no R and no Rcpp**,
depend only on Boost and the header-only parts of `odelia`, and compile and run
with no R installed at all. That is a guarantee rather than an accident, and
`.github/workflows/cpp-tests.yml` enforces it by building the whole C++ suite on
runners with no R on them.

This vignette contains no runnable R. It documents the other half of the package,
which R users never see and `plant` uses exclusively.

## The two umbrella headers, and why the extension matters

```
#include <phylloptim.hpp>    // the model. Plain C++, no R, no Rcpp.
#include <phylloptim.h>      // the R binding layer. Pulls in Rcpp.
```

⚠️ **If you are embedding the model, you want `.hpp`.** The `.h` file exists
because `RcppR6` hardwires both that name and `<phylloptim/RcppR6_pre.hpp>`, so
the R-facing umbrella had to take it and the model's had to move. A file
extension carries the whole one-way dependency rule, which is more weight than an
extension should bear — hence the banner at the top of each.

The rule: `src/` and `R/` include *downward* into `inst/include/`, never the
reverse. Nothing reachable from `<phylloptim.hpp>` includes Rcpp. The CMake
install rules encode the same split, shipping `*.hpp` and **excluding**
`phylloptim.h` and the generated `RcppR6_*.hpp`, so a non-R consumer is never
handed a header they cannot compile.

## Building

Two dependencies, both header-only: Boost (a root finder) and `odelia` (the
spline interpolator and vendored XAD). `odelia` is distributed as an R package
but the headers used here are plain C++, so a git checkout is enough.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/traitecoevo/odelia
cmake -B build -DPHYLLOPTIM_ODELIA_INCLUDE_DIR=$PWD/odelia/inst/include
cmake --build build
ctest --test-dir build          # the C++ suite, including the golden file
cmake --install build --prefix /usr/local
```

```cmake
find_package(phylloptim REQUIRED)
target_link_libraries(my_program PRIVATE phylloptim::phylloptim)
```

An INTERFACE target: headers, an include path and `cxx_std_20`, nothing to link.
`add_subdirectory()` works too if you would rather vendor it.

⚠️ **Build with optimisation on if you intend to compare against the golden
file.** Measured on macOS/arm64, `-O1`, `-O2` and `-O3` all reproduce
`tests/cpp/golden/operating_points.tsv` bit-for-bit and `-O0` does not, missing by
about 13 ULP because it declines to contract `a*b + c` into an FMA. A debug build
failing `test_golden` by ~1e-15 has found nothing.

## A solve

```cpp
#include <phylloptim.hpp>
#include <cstdio>

int main() {
  phylloptim::Leaf l;                    // default Eucalyptus saligna traits

  std::vector<double> psi_soil{2.0};     // positive magnitudes, MPa
  std::vector<double> soil_depth{1.0};   // m

  // The per-layer root RESISTANCES, per unit leaf area. If you have root carbon
  // instead, this is the architecture model that maps one to the other -- but it
  // is a helper you call, not something the solve does (#33). Supply the
  // resistances directly if that is what you have.
  const phylloptim::RootNetwork roots = phylloptim::root_network_from_carbon(
      /*root carbon per m2 LEAF*/ {20.0},
      phylloptim::layer_thickness(soil_depth), /*beta_R_H*/ 3.4e2,
      /*beta_R_V*/ 9.4e3);

  l.set_physiology(roots, /*PPFD*/ 900, psi_soil, soil_depth,
                   /*kmax*/ 3.14e-5, /*atm_vpd*/ 2.0, /*ca*/ 40.0,
                   /*leaf_temp*/ 25.0, /*atm_o2_kpa*/ 21.0,
                   /*atm_kpa*/ 101.3);
  l.find_root_collar_psi();

  std::printf("A = %.6f, gc = %.6f, psi_stem = %.6f\n",
              l.assim_colimited_, l.stom_cond_CO2_, l.opt_psi_stem_);
  return 0;
}
```

Every water potential is a **positive magnitude in MPa**, and that is asserted
rather than documented — a negative `psi_soil` is an error, not a sign convention
the model quietly accepts.

## Changing traits

The fourteen traits are replaced together, in the order `trait_table` names them:

```cpp
#include <phylloptim.hpp>
namespace p = phylloptim;

std::vector<double> theta(p::n_traits);  // fourteen, in trait_table's order
theta[p::trait_vcmax_25] = 120.0;        // p::trait_of("vcmax_25") is that index
// ...the other thirteen

phylloptim::Leaf l;
l.set_traits(theta);                     // length-checked; also a 14-argument form
```

`p::trait_table` holds the names in that order and every position has a constant
(`p::trait_vcmax_25`, `p::trait_R_d_25`, ...), so nothing indexes `theta` with a
bare integer and a misspelt name is a compile error rather than a `-1`. ⚠️ R indexes
these positions too, so reordering the table silently sets the wrong trait.

⚠️ **Supply the drivers again afterwards.** `set_traits` returns the leaf to its
just-constructed state, so `set_physiology` has to be called before the next solve.
That is not caution: `vcmax_`, `jmax_` and `R_d_` are derived from the traits inside
`set_physiology`'s temperature cache, which is keyed on leaf temperature and O₂
alone, so they are genuinely unknown until the drivers are re-supplied.

## The profit derivative at a collar potential you choose

`dprofit_droot_collar_psi(psi, &feasible)` is dprofit/dψ at a collar potential you
name rather than at the solved optimum, and `evaluate_root_collar_psi(psi)` solves
the inner problem there. plant's TF24f reads the first directly as an acclimation
rate, `dpsi/dt = k_acclim * dprofit`.

⚠️ **Pass the `feasible` flag.** `dprofit_droot_collar_psi` returns `0.0` on its
shut-down and reversed-gradient exits, and a bare zero is indistinguishable from a
stationary point — a root-find looking for `dprofit == 0` would converge onto a
shut-down state and report it as the optimum. The optional `bool*` second argument
is how the two are told apart.

## What is fast, and what is not

**Constructing a `Leaf` from R costs ~204 µs — 73 solves** — of which only ~32 µs
is the two vulnerability splines; the rest is R-side object construction. From C++
that cost is the splines alone. Reuse the object either way.

**`set_traits` is ~0.02 µs unless `stem_b`, `stem_c`, `root_b` or `root_c` move,
and 21.8 µs when one of them does**, because those four own the pre-integrated
vulnerability splines and it rebuilds one. That is 8× a solve, and most of it is the
incomplete gamma function seeding 101 knots rather than the spline machinery.

## The golden file is the contract

`tests/cpp/golden/operating_points.tsv` records 288 operating points at full
precision and is compared **bit-exactly**. It is what makes a large refactor of
this code checkable rather than hopeful, and any change that moves it is expected
to say what moved and by how much.

It is bit-exact on the platform that generated it (macOS/arm64) and compared with
per-field tolerances elsewhere, because libm's `exp`/`pow` are not
bit-reproducible across platforms. The fields split into two classes three orders
apart: `profit` is the maximum itself and well conditioned; everything else is
evaluated at the *argmax* of a flat maximum and so sqrt-amplified. **If you need a
portable check of the solve, check `profit`.**
